speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. To better understand your right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and recent memory issues, have you noticed any specific triggers for your paranoia or falls, such as lack of sleep or recent head trauma?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD).

Given the rapid progression of dementia over six months combined with acute neurological decline (right leg weakness, falls) and psychiatric symptoms, this clinical picture is highly suggestive of CJD. I am requesting results for EEG and MRI brain imaging to confirm the diagnosis.
